leagues.name: Dakar Rally (Saudi Arabia)
notes: Event-host shape: one event, not a league of clubs, so no clubs are recorded; event facts and team/vehicle-livery sponsors are recorded in unsourced. The 2027 edition runs 1-15 Jan 2027 with start and finish at King Abdullah Economic City (Rabigh) on a loop route (Arab News, 6 May 2026).

Organised by ASO (Amaury Sport Organisation) and Saudi Motorsport Company in cooperation with the Saudi Automobile and Motorcycle Federation (SAMF), under the supervision of the Ministry of Sport (Arab News, 6 May 2026; saudimotorsport.com).

Dakar has been held in Saudi Arabia since 2020 (48th edition in 2026, 3-17 Jan, Yanbu, 159 crews, 13 stages - FIA, 20 Dec 2025); 2027 is the eighth Saudi edition. Dakar director David Castera said in June 2023 the rally would stay in Saudi Arabia until at least 2029 (Motorsport.com es, 4 Jun 2023).

The 2027 route was unveiled around May 2026: about 5,320 km of timed specials, the longest Saudi-era competitive distance, with three entirely new stages (Arab News, 6 May 2026; Saudi Press Agency). Entry list not yet published; registration deadline 20 Oct 2026.

Official partners per dakar.com/en/dakar-world/partners (fetched 25 Sep 2026): host country Saudi Arabia (visitsaudi.com); institutional partners Ministry of Sport (mos.gov.sa), SAMF (samf.gov.sa), Saudi Motorsport Company (saudimotorsport.com); official partners BFGoodrich, Defender (Land Rover), Hero MotoCorp, Motul; official timekeeper TUDOR; technical partners Diverse Extreme Team and Wega; official supporter Kahoot.

Risk: as of Sep 2026 the regional security situation is worsening (Houthi attacks; the WRC's Rally Saudi Arabia planned for 12-15 Nov 2026 was cancelled and not replaced after Toyota and Hyundai travel bans). Dakar 2027 remains scheduled; re-check status before publishing.

owners.name: Amaury Group (Groupe Amaury / EPIC Editions Philippe Amaury)
owners.note: Family-owned French media and sport group that owns L'Equipe; Marie-Odile Amaury holds a majority and Aurore Amaury is CEO.

owners.name: Amaury Sport Organisation (ASO)
owners.note: Wholly owned subsidiary of the Amaury Group per ASO's own privacy policy; owns and organises the Dakar Rally, the Tour de France and about 100 events a year. Registered in Boulogne-Billancourt (SIREN 383 160 348, French company registry).

owners.name: Saudi Motorsport Company (SMC)
owners.via: operates under SAMF and the Ministry of Sport
owners.note: Founded 2021 as the dedicated entity for promoting and operating motorsport in Saudi Arabia in line with Vision 2030; chaired by HRH Prince Khalid bin Sultan Al-Abdullah Al-Faisal, who also chairs SAMF. Its own site says it operates under SAMF and the Ministry of Sport, so the state link is direct.

owners.name: Saudi Automobile and Motorcycle Federation (SAMF)
owners.note: The FIA-affiliated national motorsport federation, chaired by Prince Khalid bin Sultan Al-Abdullah Al-Faisal; cooperates on the Dakar and supervises SMC.

owners.name: Saudi Ministry of Sport
owners.note: Government ministry formed 25 Feb 2020, led by Prince Abdulaziz bin Turki Al-Faisal; supervises the Dakar Rally (Arab News, 6 May 2026: route launched 'under the supervision of the Ministry of Sport').

sponsors.name: Saudi Motorsport Company (SMC)
sponsors.note: Saudi co-organiser of the Dakar; founded 2021, operates under SAMF and the Ministry of Sport, chaired by Prince Khalid bin Sultan Al-Abdullah Al-Faisal (saudimotorsport.com).

claims.text: Human Rights Watch and 12 other human rights organisations said ASO's Dakar Rally was being used to sportswash Saudi Arabia's imprisonment of peaceful critics, noting women activists jailed for campaigning for the right to drive while the 2020 rally ran under a five-year ASO-Saudi government deal, and urging ASO to adopt a human-rights policy consistent with the UN Guiding Principles on Business and Human Rights.

source.name: Human Rights Watch - Saudi Arabia: Repressive Site for Dakar Rally
source.note: Joint statement by HRW, MENA Rights Group and 11 other organisations; also cites the Khashoggi murder and Yemen-coalition laws-of-war violations.

claims.text: As the Dakar Rally began its second Saudi edition on 2 Jan 2021, human rights organisations continued to accuse Saudi Arabia of sportswashing - using sport to divert attention from human-rights issues - while organisers defended the kingdom as host under its Vision 2030 openness push.

source.name: France 24 (AFP) - Dakar Rally set for second Saudi outing despite 'sportswashing' row
source.note: AFP wire. Site returns 403 to some automated fetchers; content confirmed via rendered fetch.

claims.text: Dakar director David Castera confirmed an agreement keeping the rally in Saudi Arabia until at least 2029, after the initial exclusive deal was set to expire after the 2024 edition, saying other countries might be added to future routes.

source.name: Motorsport.com (Spanish edition) - El Rally Dakar se quedara en Arabia Saudi hasta 2029
source.note: Castera: 'Hasta el 2029, y puede ser con otros paises tambien'. Host fee not mentioned in the article.

proposedRatings.reasoning: The Dakar's co-organiser is a Saudi state creation (founded 2021, operates under SAMF and the Ministry of Sport, chaired by a royal family member) fronting the state-hosted event named 'Dakar Rally Saudi Arabia'. The state record behind it - record executions, detained critics, the 2020-21 sportswashing objections - matches the serious tier used for Visit Saudi, Sela and the Esports Foundation.

A government ministry that supervises the Dakar in Saudi Arabia; the state's documented record (record 2024-25 executions, detained activists) puts it at serious, consistent with other Saudi state bodies in the data.

unsourced: EVENT (event-host shape; no schema yet). Dakar Rally Saudi Arabia 2027, the 49th edition, runs 1-15 Jan 2027, starting and finishing at King Abdullah Economic City (Rabigh) on a full loop route (Arab News, 6 May 2026, https://www.arabnews.com/node/2642518/sport). About 5,320 km of timed specials - the longest Saudi-era competitive distance, above the 4,903 km of 2025 - with three entirely new stages, a Red Sea focus, more sand and a marathon stage (Arab News; Saudi Press Agency https://www.spa.gov.sa/en/N2578312). The 2027 entry list was not yet published as of 25 Sep 2026; registration deadline 20 Oct 2026.

Saudi-era history: Dakar has been in Saudi Arabia since 2020; the 2026 edition (3-17 Jan, Yanbu) was the 48th, seventh Saudi edition, with 159 crews (71 W2RC-registered: 35 Ultimate, 18 Challenger, 13 SSV, 5 Stock), 13 stages, 7,994 km total, 4,840 competitive km (FIA, 20 Dec 2025, https://www.fia.com/news/saudi-arabia-prepares-host-48th-dakar-rally-and-opening-w2rc-round-new-start-venue-yanbu).

CAR-LIVERY / TEAM-LEVEL SPONSOR: Aramco fuels the Dacia Sandriders team - the four Dacia Sandrider Ultimate cars at Dakar 2026 were 'powered by ARAMCO sustainable fuel and equipped with BFGoodrich tyres' (Dacia media release, 2 Jan 2026, https://media.dacia.com/the-dacia-sandriders-awesome-foursome-determined-to-deliver-on-the-dakar-rally/?lang=eng). Dacia Sandriders won Dakar 2026 (Dacia release of 17 Jan 2026, referenced on the same media page). Drivers: Nasser Al-Attiyah/Fabian Lurquin, Sebastien Loeb/Edouard Boulanger, Lucas Moraes/Dennis Zenz, Cristina Gutierrez/Pablo Moreno. Whether Aramco continues with Dacia in 2027 is unconfirmed. Not forced into kits (car-livery shape).

Host fee: no published figure for what Saudi Arabia pays ASO or SMC to host the Dakar; the 2023 Motorsport.com interview (contract to 2029) does not mention a fee. Saudipedia describes a 10-year hosting arrangement from 2020 organised by the Ministry of Sport with SAMF (search-result only, not opened) - unverified.

Stage/broadcast presenting partners and TV broadcasters: dakar.com has an 'official broadcasters' section that could not be fully enumerated by automated fetch; needs a manual browser check (dakar.com/en/dakar-world/partners lists partner categories Host country / Institutional / Official / Timekeeper / Technical / Supporters; broadcast list lives elsewhere).
